subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted session-level `/exec` defaults continue to override global/per-agent exec config after operator config changes, or should OpenClaw make operator config authoritative on session resume and clear/ignore stale `exec*` session fields?
rationale: The code path is source-reproducible, but fixing it changes a documented session-level convenience and can affect existing operator workflows, so the security/product contract needs human ownership before implementation.

options.title: Make operator config authoritative
options.body: Recommended: global/per-agent exec policy and tool deny rules should win on resume, with focused migration or reset handling for existing stored `exec*` fields.

options.title: Keep persistent session defaults
options.body: Treat the current behavior as intentional, document the security tradeoff more explicitly, and close this as not planned after naming the supported reset/operator workflow.

options.title: Add explicit reset without changing precedence
options.body: Keep `/exec` persistence but add a visible operator reset/doctor path to clear stale session exec defaults after policy changes.

recommendation.title: Make operator config authoritative
recommendation.body: Recommended: global/per-agent exec policy and tool deny rules should win on resume, with focused migration or reset handling for existing stored `exec*` fields.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent exec/session history point to @steipete as the best available owner for the precedence/security contract decision.
